verses.text: Then Job answered:
"Yes, I know that this is true. But how can a person be right with God?
If someone wanted to argue with God, he could not answer God even once in a thousand times.
God is very wise and very strong. Who has ever fought against him and won?
He moves mountains before they know it, and turns them over in his anger.
He shakes the earth from its place and makes its pillars tremble.
He commands the sun, and it does not rise. He hides the light of the stars.
He alone spreads out the heavens and walks on the waves of the sea.
He made the Bear, Orion, the Pleiades, and the star groups of the south.
He does great things no one can understand, more amazing things than anyone can count.
When he passes by me, I cannot see him. When he goes past, I do not notice him.
If he takes something away, who can stop him? Who can say to him, 'What are you doing?'
God does not hold back his anger. Even the helpers of the monster Rahab bow down under him.
So how could I answer him? How could I choose words to argue with him?
Even if I were in the right, I could not answer him. I could only beg my judge for mercy.
Even if I called and he answered me, I do not believe he would listen to me.
He crushes me with a storm and gives me more and more wounds for no reason.
He does not let me catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
If it is a question of strength, he is the strongest! If it is a question of justice, who can call him to court?
Even if I were innocent, my own mouth would prove me guilty. Even if I had no fault, it would prove me wrong.
I have no fault, but I do not care about myself. I hate my life.
It is all the same, so I say, 'He destroys both the innocent and the wicked.'
When disaster suddenly kills people, he laughs at the suffering of the innocent.
When a land falls into the hands of the wicked, he covers the eyes of its judges. If it is not God who does this, then who is it?
My days go by faster than a runner. They fly away without seeing any happiness.
They pass by like fast boats made of reeds, like an eagle swooping down on its prey.
If I say, 'I will forget my complaint, change my sad face, and smile,'
I still dread all my suffering, because I know you will not hold me innocent.
I will be found guilty anyway, so why should I struggle for nothing?
Even if I washed myself with snow and cleaned my hands with soap,
you would throw me into a muddy pit, and even my own clothes would hate me.
God is not a human like me, so I cannot answer him or meet him in court.
If only there were someone to judge between us, to put his hand on both of us.
If only someone would take God's rod away from me, so his terror would no longer frighten me.
Then I would speak without being afraid of him. But as things are, I cannot."
